slides.title: Introduction
slides.subtitle: What is Nuclear Energy?
paragraphs: Nuclear energy is the use of nuclear reactions to produce electricity, with the vast majority of electricity from nuclear power being produced by nuclear fission of uranium and plutonium in nuclear power plants.
bullets: Label: A source of clean and sustainable energy
Label: Can be obtained from nuclear fission, nuclear decay, and nuclear fusion reactions
Label: Presently, the majority of electricity from nuclear power is produced by nuclear fission

slides.title: Key Concepts
slides.subtitle: Essential Principles of Nuclear Energy
bullets: Label: Fission - when nuclei of atoms split into several parts
Label: Fusion - when nuclei fuse together
Label: Controlled nuclear fission and fusion

slides.title: Current Situation
slides.subtitle: Trends, Facts, and Examples
paragraphs: Nuclear energy is a significant source of electricity worldwide, with many countries relying on it for their power needs.

slides.subtitle: Trade-Offs in Nuclear Energy Development
